tool_args.new_string:
The full metric disagreement (L4 vs.\ L63, a 59-layer gap) is the superposition of a geometric artifact on the crossing-rate side and a real safety signal on the threshold-based side.

\paragraph{R1-8B (Llama).} The Llama-based model shows stronger label dependence: crossing rate scatters from L0 to mean L$10.7 \pm 4.8$ under random labels (0\% shallow), unlike QwQ-32B where it retains shallow preference. Threshold-based metrics degenerate entirely---precision and inverse FPR select L0 in all 10 repeats with zero variance, indicating random labels destroy discriminative signal rather than merely redistributing it. The real-CP disagreement (L0 vs.\ L23, a 23-layer gap) vanishes completely under random labels.

\paragraph{Cross-architecture summary.} The metric disagreement requires genuine safety labels in both architectures, but the mechanism differs: in QwQ-32B, crossing-rate shallow preference reflects representation geometry (label-independent cosine compression), while in R1-8B even crossing-rate layer selection is label-dependent. The geometric component of the crossing-rate bias is thus Qwen-specific rather than a universal property of transformer representations.

Limitations

703

Single dataset. All probe experiments use one
dataset (HarmThoughts (Kakkar et al., 2026)); the
geometric precondition (shallow-layer compression) is confirmed on AdvBench (Zou et al., 2023b)
(Sections C and C.1), but CP-dependent claims
rely on HarmThoughts, which provides step-level
CP annotations derived from manual inspection
of reasoning chains. The dataset spans multiple
harmful categories (e.g., violence, fraud, illegal activities) but we do not stratify results by category;
categories with longer average reasoning chains or
earlier CPs may exhibit different probe dynamics.
CP positions range from early to late within traces,
though the distribution is right-skewed (most CPs
occur in the first half of reasoning). Annotation
granularity (step-level vs. token-level), category
distribution, and annotator team composition may
all influence which layers carry discriminative signal and how strongly metric bias manifests. Interannotator agreement (IAA) was not computed for
these annotations, though an LLM-based proxy on
AdvBench achieved κ=0.606 (Section J.1). Random annotation noise would attenuate effect sizes
symmetrically, making our estimates conservative;
systematic noise (e.g., consistent early or late CP
placement) could bias layer selection or inflate
modality differences. Without IAA, we cannot
distinguish these cases, so our conclusions may
not transfer to independently annotated corpora.
Generalization to other jailbreak datasets, attack
taxonomies, or multilingual settings is untested.

**R1-8B Random-Label Control 结果 + 论文集成完成**

## 实验结果

R1-8B (Llama, 209 traces, 25 layers, 10 random-label repeats):

| 指标 | Real-CP layer | Random-CP mean layer | Shallow% |
|------|--------------|---------------------|----------|
| Crossing rate | L0 | 10.7±4.8 | 0% |
| CR-composite | L0 | 13.7±6.7 | 0% |
| Precision | L23 | 0.0±0.0 (degenerate) | 100%† |
| Inv. FPR | L13 | 0.0±0.0 (degenerate) | 100%† |

†degenerate: 所有 10 repeats 都选 L0，零方差，signal 被彻底摧毁

## 跨架构对比

| | QwQ-32B (Qwen) | R1-8B (Llama) |
|---|---|---|
| Crossing-rate under random | 保持 shallow (100% L≤10, geometric) | 散射到中间层 (0% shallow) |
| Precision under random | 散射 (mean L34) | 退化到 L0 (signal destroyed) |
| Metric disagreement replicates? | No | No |
| Geometric component? | Yes (crossing-rate) | No |

**核心发现**：metric disagreement 在两种架构下都需要真实 CP labels，但机制不同——QwQ-32B 的 crossing-rate 浅层偏好有 geometric 成分（label-independent cosine compression），R1-8B 的 crossing-rate 也是 label-dependent。Geometric bias 是 Qwen-specific。
